name: Wrap / mid-rise multifamily
summary: 4-5 story Type III/V wood-frame apartments wrapped around a free-standing precast or post-tensioned parking deck (the 'Texas donut'). Cost sits between garden and podium: the garage (~1.3 spaces/unit at ~$30k/space) adds ~15% to the per-unit hard cost, plus elevators and interior corridors. Product-specific data are thin - two developer/educational ranges, older architect ranges and broad RLB/RSMeans multifamily bands - so the mid leans on ratios to garden and podium.

typicalSize.method: Wrap projects are typically one large building around a 4-6 level garage; 250-450 units is the common deal size in Sun Belt metros (judgment; Apers/LandSouth describe the type without a unit count).

sfPerPrimaryUnit.method: Gross residential + amenity SF per unit, excluding the garage. Census median new rental unit = 1,000 net SF (e12); wrap units average ~850-950 net SF and interior-corridor efficiency ~80-85% => ~1,050-1,150 gross.

primaryUnitsPerAcre.method: LandSouth and Apers both give 50-90 units/acre; mid set toward the lower half where most suburban wraps land.

parkingPerPrimaryUnit.method: Apers: 1.2-1.5 (and ~1.0-1.5 'Texas Donut') spaces per unit in the structured deck; mid 1.3.

perPrimaryUnit.method: Per-unit = perSF x sfPerPrimaryUnit: mid $240 x 1,100 = $264k (rounded $265k); low ~$195-200 x 1,000 = ~$200k; high ~$300-310 x 1,200 = ~$360k. Garage check: 1.3 spaces x WGI median $29,900/space (e10, 2024) ~= $39k/unit (~15% of mid). Florida mid-rise LIHTC hard-cost factor $284-311k/unit (e11, a cap) brackets the mid.

perSF.method: Per gross residential SF with the garage cost spread over it. 2026 evidence: LandSouth and Apers $200-275 (e1, e2; midpoint ~$237); RLB all-multifamily in Dallas/Austin $190-285 (e7, e8) and 18-city median $225-410 (e6); RSMeans 4-7 story $210-475 (e5). Mid $240 = LandSouth/Apers midpoint, ~1.30x the garden mid ($185), consistent with older ratio evidence: MFE 2016 wrap $175-225/RSF vs podium $250-300 (e3) and EVstudio 2018 podium/wrap vs walk-up ~1.13x (e4) before garage. High reflects higher-cost metros (RAND CA/TX wrap ratio 2.1, e9).

scope.notes: Contractor price incl. general conditions and OH&P, the parking structure (~1.3 spaces/unit), on-site work, courtyard amenities and elevators; perSF is per gross residential SF (garage area excluded from the SF but its cost included). Excludes land, soft costs, FF&E, off-sites, impact/tap fees, financing.

qualityTiers.method: Same finish/amenity spread as garden-multifamily (EVstudio amenity premium ~+7%, e4; Terrapin market vs affordable ~+25% in the garden file), slightly compressed because the garage and structure don't scale with finish level.

systemSplit.method: Derived from the garden split (RAND Table 3.4 mapping, see garden-multifamily.json) with adjustments for the wrap: +7 pts concrete (03) for the precast/PT garage and slab-on-grade, +1.5 pts elevators (14), +0.6 pts sprinklers/standpipes (21), +0.6 pts HVAC (23, corridor conditioning), -3.4 pts framing (06), -3.7 pts site divisions (31-33, smaller site, no surface lots), small reductions elsewhere for the larger shell. Verify against a wrap GMP schedule of values.

lineItems.name: Wrapped parking structure (precast or PT, above grade)

cost.method: WGI 2024 national median for a parking structure $29,900/space (mid); low/high = typical +/-15-25% spread for simple precast vs. PT decks with ramps tied into residential corridors (judgment).

lineItems.notes: Carve-out; already inside the wrap baseline.

lineItems.name: Passenger elevators (4-5 stop, MRL traction or hydraulic)

cost.method: Derived: installed 4-5 stop passenger elevator ~ $130-250k each (2026); ~1 car per 80-100 units plus a service car.
Derived: resort-style pool, deck, cabanas and courtyard landscaping over podium/grade for a 300-unit wrap (2026 judgment).

lineItems.name: Ground-floor retail shell (cold dark shell)

cost.method: Derived: retail shell space within a wood/concrete residential building ~ $150-275/SF (2026), excluding TI.

lineItems.notes: Optional - some urban wraps include street retail.

perPrimaryUnit.method: Derived: lobby, clubroom, fitness, co-working, pool furniture ~ $500-900k for ~330 units (2026).

pctOfHard.method: RAND market-rate soft/hard 0.19 (TX/CO) to 0.33 (CA), incl. financing (e13); Brookings 20-30% of total cost (e14). Mid slightly above garden (0.22) for structural/garage engineering and longer schedule; excludes construction interest. | Second pass (2026-10-24, main session): Reduced 5 points: RAND-based, includes developer costs and fees. The engine adds impact & tap fees, the developer fee and construction financing as their own lines (docs/BUDGET_ENGINE.md §5), so this bucket must exclude them.

softCosts.notes: Impact/tap fees modeled separately (RAND: <$1k/unit TX, ~$12k CO, ~$29k CA).

hard.method: Derived industry norm for mid-rise wood/garage projects under GMP.

perPrimaryUnit.method: Hard low $200k x 1.12 ~= $225k; hard high $360k x 1.42 ~= $510k; rounded.
